_meta.indication: Treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma and disease progression following ipilimumab and, if BRAF V600 mutation positive, a BRAF inhibitor (accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and durability of response)

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, randomized (1:1), dose-comparative, activity-estimating cohort (Part B2)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma refractory to two or more doses of ipilimumab (3 mg/kg or higher) and, if BRAF V600 mutation-positive, a BRAF or MEK inhibitor
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR) per RECIST 1.1 by blinded independent central review, and duration of response
pivotal_trials.n: 173 patients randomized to KEYTRUDA 2 mg/kg (n=89) or 10 mg/kg (n=84) every 3 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 24% (95% CI: 15, 34) in the 2 mg/kg arm (1 complete response and 20 partial responses); among 21 responders, 86% had ongoing responses (durations 1.4+ to 8.5+ months)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were fatigue (47%), cough (30%), nausea (30%), pruritus (30%), rash (29%), decreased appetite (26%), constipation (21%), arthralgia (20%), and diarrhea (20%); serious risks are immune-mediated reactions including pneumonitis (2.9% of 411 melanoma patients). KEYTRUDA was discontinued for adverse reactions in 6% of patients.
target_moa: Humanized monoclonal antibody that binds the PD-1 receptor and blocks its interaction with PD-L1 and PD-L2, releasing PD-1 pathway-mediated inhibition of the anti-tumor T-cell immune response

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee; the Division did not obtain ODAC advice because the safety profile was acceptable and the efficacy outcome measures were similar to those for previously approved accelerated-approval melanoma products
